stemMd: A shop will introduce reusable delivery crates to reduce packaging waste. Which finding most seriously challenges the expectation of a net reduction in packaging waste?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The crates are easier to stack.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The shop will print its logo on the crates.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Some customers like the appearance of the crates.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Most crates are discarded after one delivery, and each contains more material than the disposable packaging it replaces.

explanationMd: The proposal depends on actual reuse, not merely the ability to reuse. If heavier crates are normally discarded immediately, the substitution can increase rather than decrease the amount of packaging thrown away.

distractorRationale.a: Stackability does not establish the amount discarded.
distractorRationale.c: Appearance is irrelevant to net waste.
distractorRationale.e: Technical reusability does not establish actual reuse.
distractorRationale.b: Branding does not quantify discarded material.
